header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jared Lin (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (SpruceFin Head of Data), Ethan Cole (SpruceFin CTO), Priya Nair (SpruceFin Security)
summary: POC scoping for SpruceFin focusing on data handling: PII identification/redaction, prompt storage policy, retention settings, and benchmark sizing. Customer prefers Private (VPC) deployment with KMS integration and strict audit logs. Agreed 4-week pilot timeline; success criteria to include latency and cost targets plus zero plaintext PII retention.
transcript:
[00:00] Jared: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jared from Redwood. quick intros?
[00:12] Marta: hi, Marta here, head of data at SpruceFin. thanks.
[00:18] Ethan: Ethan, CTO. we'll probably talk about private hosting a bunch.
[00:22] Priya: Priya, security. focused on PII and auditability.
[00:26] Samira: Samira Patel, solutions engineer, i'll run through the benchmark plan and data flow.
[00:35] Jared: goal for today is to lock down success criteria and the data handling boundaries for the POC — what you want us to log, what we must redact, retention TTLs, and sizing for the test workload.
[01:05] Marta: high level — we ingest customer conversations, payment metadata, and some identifiers. we need to ensure nothing PHI/PII is stored in plaintext in the prompt logs. also want to validate latency for real-time flows.
[01:27] Ethan: for sizing: our peak concurrency is about 120 rps for inference, but average is closer to 30. tokens per request vary — compressed user msg ~80 tokens, model reply ~120 tokens.
[01:40] Samira: ok that's helpful, so for the POC we'll simulate mixed lengths. recommended baseline test: 10k requests, mix: 60% short (<=100 tokens), 30% medium (100-400), 10% long (>400). we'll include KV-cache warmup runs.
[02:05] Priya: can you explain the logging model? when you say logs, do you keep full prompts? hashed?
[02:15] Samira: good q. by default Redwood's hosted API keeps request/response artifacts for 30 days for debugging; for Private you control retention. for the pilot we can set retention to 7 days and enable redaction at ingestion. redaction can be rule-based (regex) or token-based PII detector. note: the PII detector isn't perfect — it's ML-driven so we usually recommend an allowlist/denylist for critical fields.
[02:45] Marta: we need zero plaintext for account numbers and ssn-like. hashed values are fine if salted and you can prove reversible only through our KMS.
[02:58] Jared: yep, we support encrypted prompt storage behind customer KMS in the Private deployment. so the flow is client -> redwood private endpoint (VPC) -> encrypted object store with KMS CMKs. audit logs show access events, and content can be masked at ingestion if you prefer no raw persist.
[03:20] Ethan: network wise we need to see a diagram of egress, subnets etc before greenlight.
[03:26] Samira: we'll include a network diagram. quick note on redaction: we can do inline redaction (strip out PII from the prompt before hitting the model) or post-hoc redaction (store raw, redact in logs). you asked for zero plaintext — inline redaction is safer but sometimes impacts model quality because you lose context.
[03:55] Priya: quality vs privacy tradeoff — yes that's our headache. can you run a quality regression test with redaction turned on?
[04:03] Samira: absolutely, part of the benchmark will include "with-redaction" and "no-redaction" cohorts and we'll compute delta on intent accuracy and hallucination rate.
[04:18] Marta: what about partial pseudonymization? replace CI with stable tokens so downstream dedup works.
[04:24] Samira: stable tokenization is supported — we can salt the hash per-customer using your KMS key. that gives re-identification only if you hold the key.
[04:33] Ethan: timeline? how long for infra and run?
[04:37] Jared: propose a four-week POC: week1 network & IAM setup, week2 deploy model and run smoke tests, week3 run benchmarks (10k + warmups), week4 analyze results and iterate. flexible but that is what we usually do.
[05:00] Marta: sounds good. success criteria for us are 95th pctl latency under 500ms for our typical path and end-to-end latency for chat flows < 700ms. cost target: under $0.18 per 1k tokens for the POC workload. and of course no plaintext sensitive fields in logs.
[05:24] Samira: to be clear we can measure p50/p95/p99 on token-level and end-to-end. our standard benchmark harness will capture CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, and per-request token billing estimates.
[05:42] Priya: auditability — we need immutable audit logs with SSO user IDs for any access to logs or config changes. can you integrate with our SAML IdP?
[05:54] Jared: yes, SAML SSO + RBAC supported. for Private we'll integrate with your IdP and map groups -> roles. audit logs go to your logging endpoint (SIEM) in near real-time. we'll share sample CloudWatch/ELK forwarder config.
[06:12] Ethan: and encryption at rest?
[06:16] Samira: KMS integration for disk and object storage. we support BYOK with customer-managed CMK. also HSM-backed key option if you require FIPS/HSM.
[06:28] Marta: one subtlety: our legal wants proof that transient storage (e.g., model context when tokenizing) doesn't persist. how do you show that?
[06:38] Samira: we can provide runtime instrumentation and a small benchmark that demonstrates no writes to persistent stores during inference, and we can run a memory-scan audit with your security team. that usually satisfies legal. we'll also provide code snippets showing a no-persist flag in the runtime config.
[06:58] Priya: ok good. bench specifics — Samira you suggested KV-cache warmups, how much warmup is typical?
[07:06] Samira: depends on model and sequence length. for our Llama-2-esque family we usually do 5k warmup requests with similar length distribution, then the 10k measured run. warmup ensures KV cache is populated and we get realistic latency numbers. we'll include both cold-start and warm paths.
[07:25] Ethan: concurrency — you mentioned batching earlier. will batching harm our 95th pctl?
[07:31] Samira: batching helps amortize cost but increases tail latency for single-user interactive flows. our routing policy can do mixed mode: latency-sensitive requests bypass batching and go to low-latency nodes, while background bulk ops are batched. we can configure based on route headers.
[07:51] Marta: for the POC we'll want one route with low-latency config and one route for cheaper batched inference to compare.
[07:58] Jared: noted. also want to surface model variants — if a cheaper quantized model shows similar quality we can fallback under load to keep SLOs.
[08:09] Priya: fallback policy must not leak different logging behaviors — logs must remain consistent across model variants.
[08:16] Samira: will ensure consistent telemetry. logs will include model variant id, but content logging obeys the same retention/redaction rules.
[08:25] Marta: can we get a sample prompt dataset? we have privacy concerns about actual customer messages.
[08:32] Samira: yes, provide a synthetic set or we can mask your dataset on ingestion. for benchmark comparability we prefer a realistic synthetic set derived from your stats (token distribution, entity types).
[08:45] Ethan: testing weights — we also want to include a spike test: 2x peak for 10 minutes to observe autoscale behavior.
[08:53] Samira: makes sense, we'll include controlled spike windows and a failover exercise to validate fallback to cheaper region/variant.
[09:02] Priya: regarding retention policies — we want prompt logs auto-deleted at 7 days, but metadata and audit trails kept for 90 days. is that configurable?
[09:11] Samira: yes, retention per artifact type is configurable in Private. request/response payload TTLs, telemetry logs, and audit logs can have independent TTLs.
[09:24] Marta: any caveats with redaction + retention? e.g., if you redact inline, do you ever keep a raw copy in backups?
[09:30] Samira: no backups of raw when inline redaction is on. post-hoc redaction could leave raw in backups unless you explicitly disable raw backups. we'll default to no raw backups for this POC.
[09:44] Ethan: benchmarks — let's list the exact metrics we'll consider success on: p95 latency, p99 maybe as a stretch, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy delta with redaction, and error rate under spike.
[09:59] Samira: agreed. I'll put those in the benchmark doc with thresholds and measurement windows.
[10:06] Jared: security review items: SOC2, encryption, SSO, KMS, data residency. Priya what do you need to see in the security pack?
[10:16] Priya: SOC2 report, architecture diagrams, penetration test summary, list of third-party subprocessors, dataflow for PII and retention settings, and a sample runbook for incident response.
[10:30] Jared: we'll attach SOC2 and pen test summary and a subprocessors list. note: some of the underlying infra is third-party cloud, we will call that out.
[10:39] Marta: about region/residency — we need data egress to stay in-us-east-1. is that supported?
[10:43] Samira: yes, Private can be deployed in your VPC in us-east-1; we'll keep storage and logs in-region. for hosted endpoints we'll route to region-specific clusters but for POC Private is recommended.
[10:55] Ethan: ok good. would like to measure cost numbers across quantization levels — 8-bit vs 4-bit. can you provide guidance?
[11:04] Samira: we'll run model variants including int8 and 4-bit quantized where supported. cost delta typically 2-3x but quality needs to be validated. we'll include the quant choices in the benchmark matrix.
[11:18] Priya: can we also capture how often de-identified stable tokens are re-identified in logs? we want to track possible correlation risk.
[11:27] Samira: yes we'll include a re-identification risk metric — count of stable tokens that map to the same original across the dataset, controlled by salt and key.
[11:36] Marta: are there any limitations in Redwood runtime around tokenization for non-utf8 chars? we have multi-lingual inputs for some clients.
[11:44] Samira: runtime handles UTF-8; for legacy encodings we'd recommend normalization pre-ingest. we'll capture error rates for nonstandard chars in the bench.
[11:54] Ethan: what's the on-call support model during the POC?
[11:58] Jared: standard is Slack + on-call pager for infra issues. for Private we offer a designated SE for the POC window and a weekly status.
[12:07] Marta: cost estimation — Samira you said you'll provide a per-token cost estimate based on measured throughput?
[12:13] Samira: yes, we'll produce a per-1k token cost projection factoring in batching and idle utilization observed during runs.
[12:21] Priya: last — legal wants to see contract clause for data processing: who is processor, who controller, liabilities. can you send a sample term sheet?
[12:30] Jared: yep, i'll pass a redwood sample term sheet and our data processing addendum.
[12:36] Marta: ok to recap — 4-week POC, Private in us-east-1, 10k measured requests with warmups, redaction and no-raw-backup policy, retention 7d for payloads/90d metadata, KMS BYOK, benchmarks include p95/p99/cost/accuracy delta + spike test.
[12:58] Ethan: and we want the benchmark plan and network diagram by next week.
[13:03] Samira: i'll put the plan in a google sheet and share link, include synthetic dataset generator and runner.
[13:09] Priya: please make the security docs easy to consume — summary + full docs.
[13:13] Jared: will do. any other questions?
[13:17] Marta: none from me.
[13:18] Ethan: none.
[13:19] Priya: no. thanks.
[13:21] Jared: great — we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the onboarding. thanks all.
[13:30] -- End of Recording --

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings ("K V cache" sometimes transcribed instead of KV-cache; "Redwood Dedicate" appears once). Shared artifacts: benchmark plan (link to internal doc), security pack (link), network diagram (link).
